event.summary: Host shutdown test drops the missing/stale version-hold oracle
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: the tests no longer protect the rule that a running session is unprotected until its own version hold is published; shutdown tests can pass if any mark, or no mark, is incorrectly accepted. This is a lost regression oracle, not a claim of a product failure. The assigned patch deletes an_orderly_stop_waits_for_new_windows_to_hold_their_version, which asserted false for an absent mark and for a mark with another pid, then true for the owned child's mark. Its replacement the_stop_wait_covers_launches_still_starting at 25980–26019 writes the correct child pid at 26005–26009 BEFORE tracking the terminal at 26010 and dropping the starting count at 26011. While the mark is absent, the terminal is not yet in pending_holds and the starting count alone keeps the loop waiting. Every examination of a tracked running terminal therefore sees the correct mark; accepting missing/stale marks would produce the same true result. The other surviving hold-wait test at 26070 onward only checks refusal of a launch after an empty wait has ended. A full core.rs symbol search finds no other hold_settled/track_pending_hold test exercising an absent or stale mark at the tracked-terminal boundary. SPEC_impl.md, Terminal host, line 2230: The orderly stop's hold wait compares the "held" mark with the child's pid. core.rs hold_settled at 7798 onward still correctly compares equality. That current production correctness refutes a product-regression claim but cannot replace the deleted negative tests. The tmux-blocked-probe race stimulus is retired because the host probe is synchronous; the mark identity/absence boundary still exists and does not need a blocked server to exercise. Suggested fix: keep a live owned test-host child tracked while the mark is absent and then stale, assert the wait cannot settle (or directly assert hold_settled is false), and assert true only after the matching mark is installed. Establish child liveness at those observations. Suggested bucket: other (test coverage regression). Could-be-highest: no established product security or user-work-loss route; no product malfunction claimed. Confidence: confirmed from source; no execution. proposed_drop: false for this remaining test oracle; the earlier dismissal is revised. possible_cover: none; excluded coverage sources not searched. Material caveat: does not restore the obsolete asynchronous tmux probe stimulus, nor claim an observed pruning/start failure. Original consequence considered remains shutdown failing to protect a just-starting session's version, but source establishes only weakened regression protection.

event.summary: OMP owner-exit test no longer establishes that its owner exited
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: the test intended to protect Restart after an OMP agent exits can now pass without establishing that the agent exited. This is a test-evidence regression, not an observed product failure. Details: spawn_one (22931–22967) now calls start_in_host, which registers OwnedRuntime { child: None, group: pid } (22813–22818). kill_owner (23048–23052) calls teardown, which sends a group SIGKILL and waits only for Some(child) (22545–22551). With the host child there is no wait and the signal return is ignored (22581–22586). omp_accepted_capture_survives_owner_exit_and_reload calls kill_owner at 24056 and immediately asserts the offer 'after the owner exits' at 24057–24060, without reading the runtime/reporter identities or waiting for them to become gone/zombie. session_snapshot (7448–7487), used by offer (23228–23238), reads only the stored row and computes the offer; it provides no exit barrier. The subsequent reopen does not retroactively establish the premise of the first assertion. The preceding fixture's Some(child) path called Child::wait before returning, so migration removes an actual synchronization point. Test-review contract: 'Assert the fixture premise before the action or measurement that depends on it. A successful setup command alone does not establish the state the assertion needs.' SPEC.md, Durability and resume, promises sessions and per-session conversation capture survive supervisor restarts, and SPEC_impl.md Terminal host states that the host reaps its own child; this test explicitly promises its assertion occurs after both owner and reporter are gone. Fix direction: retain runtime and reporter start identities and await wait_pid_gone (already present at 22633–22656) for both before the owner-exit assertion, proving the fixture live beforehand. Suggested bucket: other, confined to test evidence. Could-be-highest: no established product security or loss-of-work route; this finding does not claim a broken Restart. Confidence: confirmed by source, with no runtime observation. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none; excluded coverage sources not searched. Material caveat: SIGKILL will ordinarily take effect quickly; the defect is the missing readiness oracle and ignored failure, not proof that this test currently fails or that admitted captures are lost.
